title: Music Industry Moves: Jesse Jo Stark Signs With WME, Rebecca Allen Steps Down at Universal Music U.K.
description:
Singer-songwriter-actress and Chrome Hearts co-creative director Jesse Jo Stark has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas.

	St
body:
Singer-songwriter-actress and Chrome Hearts co-creative director Jesse Jo Stark has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas.

	Stark’s new album “Muse” is out Nov. 6, which follows dates opening for or performing with Post Malone, Guns N’ Roses and Jane’s Addiction, as well as multiple festival appearances. In addition to her work at Chrome Hearts, Stark also helms the clothing line Deadly Doll.


	+ Veteran music executive Rebecca Allen is leaving Universal Music Group U.K. after 27 years, according to Music Week. She will continue in an advisory role at UMG.
	

	Following the merger of EMI and Island in July 2024, Allen was appointed as president of the new Audience & Media division, and subsequently promoted to the newly-formed, “first-of-its-kind” leadership role of chief artist and strategy officer in December 2025. Previously, she was president and later co-president of the relaunched EMI (alongside Jo Charrington), following her role as president of Decca from 2017 to 2020 – becoming the first female president at a Universal Music U.K. label.

	“I leave enormously proud of what we’ve created together, grateful for the friendships, the adventures, the lessons and the laughter, and for 27 years that have shaped me in more ways than I probably even realise yet,” Allen wrote in a farewell letter to staff, per MW. “It’s been quite a ride. I can’t thank you all enough for being on this journey with me. Love to you all.”

	+ Sony Music Publishing Colombia has entered into a global catalog administration agreement with the Estate of acclaimed Colombian singer, songwriter and accordionist Omar Geles, one of the most influential artists to work in vallenato music. The agreement encompasses more than three-hundred celebrated works penned by the Latin-Grammy nominated songwriter including the vallenato anthem “Cuatro Rosas,” as well as classics such as “A Blanco y Negro,” “Tu Hombre Soy Yo” and “Tarde lo Conocí.”
	

	“In the name of my family and the Omar Geles state, we want to extend our most sincere gratitude for opening your doors and allow us to be part of the Sony Music Publishing family,” said Maren García. “We hope to build a relationship based in trust, respect, and the commitment of continuing to take Omar Geles’ legacy to new generations. Thanks for making us feel at home since the first moment and for continuing to write the history of the legacy of my eternal love, a legacy that will continue to live in each one of his songs.”

	Jorge Mejía, President and CEO, Latin America and U.S. Latin, Sony Music Publishing said, “Omar Geles was not only a defining voice in vallenato music, but one of the great songwriters of his generation. It is a true honor to partner with his family to preserve, promote and expand his legacy, ensuring that his songs continue to inspire audiences around the world for generations to come.”

	+ The Music Publishers Association, the U.K. trade body representing music publishers, has named Faber Music CEO Richard King as its new Board Chair for a three-year term, following a vote by its Board of Directors. He succeeds Paulette Long OBE, who remains an MPA Board Director following the conclusion of her term as Chair.

	Having served as CEO of leading independent music publisher Faber Music since 1999, King brings more than 25 years of publishing leadership to the role, with experience spanning classical, film and TV, pop and printed music. He previously served as an MPA Director from 2002 to 2019 before rejoining the Board in 2022. He was a PRS director for 18 years to 2022, a Director of PRS Foundation for 9 years to 2024 and has been a Director of PML since its inception in 2012. King will work alongside Peter Jackson, who joined the MPA as Managing Director in July.

	“I’m looking forward to building on the great work of Paulette and the MPA executive team, particularly by using my experience as a music publisher to further amplify our sector’s voice on the issues that matter most to members,” King said. “There is plenty to build on. The Government’s recently announced Plan for Music and new National Plan for Music Education are welcome steps, but we need to ensure these initiatives lead to meaningful, sustained long-term change. At a time of enormous change, it is more important than ever that music publishers have a strong and unified voice.”
	

	Paul Clements, CEO of the MPA Group, added, “Richard has been an important voice within the MPA for many years and I know he will bring fresh thinking, challenge and real ambition to the role of Chair. Peter has already made a huge impact since joining us, bringing new energy and ideas to the team and a clear vision for how we can do even more for our members.

	“I’d also like to thank Paulette for her outstanding leadership and contribution as Chair. With Richard leading the Board and Peter driving the MPA forward day-to-day, we have a brilliant team in place for this next chapter.”

title: Joni Mitchell Sworn In as a U.S. Citizen, Capping ‘a Journey That Began 62 Years Ago’
description: When the New York Times ran a list of the greatest living American songwriters earlier this year, the ranking was greeted with a lot of reader fla
body:
When the New York Times ran a list of the greatest living American songwriters earlier this year, the ranking was greeted with a lot of reader flack for not including Joni Mitchell. The newspaper’s explanation at the time was that Mitchell was — and remained — a Canadian citizen, despite residing primarily in California, thus the exclusion.

	Now, the Times may need to update and amend the list after all, because the legendary singer-songwriter is now a U.S. citizen.

	On her Instagram Tuesday morning, Mitchell posted a photograph of herself, smiling as she held an American flag, standing in front of dual United States and Department of Homeland Security flags. Along with that, she posted a short video of herself being applauded as she was called up to be sworn in as a citizen.

	Her simple caption: “A journey that began 62 years ago.”


	No further information was immediately forthcoming from Mitchell or her reps about the surprise move to dual citizenship after six-plus decades.

	Some may wonder why Mitchell picked now, of all times, to officially align herself with the U.S., given how many musicians of her generation and ilk have come out with statements suggesting that the Trump era has not been America’s proudest moment. But there’s a possibility that the current climate had something, or everything, to do with her decision.

	Two years ago, in an appearance fronting a “Joni Jam” at the Hollywood Bowl, Mitchell blurted out “Fuck Donald Trump,” then added, “I wish I could vote…I’m a Canadian. I’m one of those lousy immigrants.”


	Mitchell was born Roberta Joan Anderson in 1943 in Fort McLeod, Alberta. Her family moved to Saskatoon when she was 9. She enrolled at Calgary’s Alberta College of Art in 1963. Biographies generally cite her move to the U.S. as occurring in 1965, when she married Chuck Mitchell and the couple moved to Detroit, both becoming part of the folk scene there. She made her first appearance in New York at the Gaslight the following year, then moved to Chelsea in 1967 following a marital separation. She headed west to the Laurel Canyon area of Los Angeles in 1968, then bought a home in Bel Air in 1975.

	But she maintained close Canadian ties and, amid her U.S. adventures, set up residency in British Columbia around the time “Blue” was released in 1971. Most recently, she has been known to host private “Joni jams” with fellow musicians in the Santa Barbara area.


	Mitchell suffered a brain aneurysm in 2015 and was considered retired from public performance for years after that, but made a remarkable, if gradual, recovery that led to her performing at the Newport Folk Festival in 2022 as part of an all-star “Joni Jam” organized by Brandi Carlile, followed by similar group performances at the Gorge in Washington state in 2023 and the Hollywood Bowl in 2024.

schema.headline: Joni Mitchell Sworn In as a U.S. Citizen, Capping ‘a Journey That Began 62 Years Ago’

title: Ari Emanuel and Ben Persky’s Podcast ‘Rushmore’ Returns for Season 2 With Guests Including Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld
description: Ari Emanuel, executive chairman of WME Group and exec chair and CEO of TKO Group, is back to debate GOATs with his friend and music manager Ben Per
body:
Ari Emanuel, executive chairman of WME Group and exec chair and CEO of TKO Group, is back to debate GOATs with his friend and music manager Ben Persky — with a parade of high-profile guests — in a new season of their podcast “Rushmore.”

	“Rushmore” Season 2 will be available to watch on YouTube and listen on all major podcast platforms. (Season 1 initially premiered exclusively on Elon Musk’s X last year.)


	According to Emanuel and Persky, the idea behind “Rushmore” is to go beyond the typical GOAT (greatest of all time) arguments to tap into the insights — and personal stories — from top figures across sports, entertainment, media, fashion, music, gaming and more.
	

	Season 2 premieres Oct. 20, kicking off with NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and sports analyst Pat McAfee joining Emanuel and Persky to debate who belongs on the Mount Rushmore of NFL comebacks.

	The season’s second episode, airing a week later on Oct. 27 in tandem with the kickoff of the NBA season, brings together Shaquille O’Neal and Kevin Durant to tackle another perennial debate: the greatest starting five in NBA history. Following the first two episodes, Rushmore will move to a bi-weekly release cadence.

	Later this season, Larry David and Jerry Seinfeld will join Emanuel and Persky for a special episode about comedy GOATs taped during the Netflix Is a Joke festival in May 2026.

	“Everyone has their own Rushmore, and everyone thinks theirs is right,” Emanuel said in a statement. “Season 2 turns up the volume with bigger debates, bigger personalities and even more people willing to tell us why we’re wrong.”
	

	Added Persky: “The debate is what gets us started, but the fun is in the stories and history that paint the conversation. “When you dig into what makes people the greatest, with the foremost experts of those fields, you get world-class perspective about the things we all obsess over.”

	Season 2 of “Rushmore” is presented with media and podcast company nativ.ly and produced by Pantheon Media Group. It’s shot primarily from WME Group’s newly renovated Beverly Hills headquarters. 

	The return of the podcast comes a month after Emanuel’s new memoir “Roll the Calls” was released Sept. 22. In the 432-page tome, Emanuel chronicles his rise from the CAA mailroom to become one of the most powerful people in entertainment and sports.

	The first season of “Rushmore” comprised 15 episodes, with guests including Tom Brady, Peyton Manning, Anna Wintour, Elon Musk, Rick Rubin, Dana White, Jimmy Iovine, Bob Costas, Al Michaels, Doris Kearns Goodwin, Jon Meacham, Jeff Koons, Jeffrey Deitch, Inez van Lamsweerde, Edward Enninful, Bobby Kotick and Reggie Miller.

	Watch the trailer for Season 2 of “Rushmore”:


	Pictured top (l. to r.:) Ben Persky, Larry David, Jerry Seinfeld, Ari Emanuel

title: BondIt, Buffalo 8 and Sandaled Kid Productions Team Up on High-Concept Horror Film Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
BondIt Media Capital, Buffalo 8 Distribution and Sandaled Kid Productions have partnered on a new slate of horror films.

	The partnership will dev
body:
BondIt Media Capital, Buffalo 8 Distribution and Sandaled Kid Productions have partnered on a new slate of horror films.

	The partnership will develop three commercial, high-concept horror films. BondIt will finance the slate, while Buffalo 8 will release the titles. Sandaled Kid Productions will focus on development and production of the projects.

	“This partnership brings together companies with complementary strengths and a shared belief in bold, commercial genre filmmaking,” James Cullen Bressack, Sandaled Kid Productions founder, said in a statement. “We wanted to build a slate that feels fresh, marketable and genuinely scary, while giving each film the opportunity to stand out in a crowded marketplace.”
	

	The deal was negotiated by Bressack and Matthew Helderman, CEO and co-founder of BondIt and Buffalo 8. Bressack and Helderman will both serve as executive producers for the three films.


	“James is a longtime collaborator with our teams at both BondIt and Buffalo 8 — and we’re excited for another adventure with him as we target the release of these films for 2027,” Helderman said in a statement. “This genre slate of original films reflects our continued expansion and focus on greenlighting new commercial projects for VOD audiences.”

	Additional details, including titles, filmmakers and production schedules, have yet to be announced.

	Helderman founded Buffalo 8 in 2010 as an independent media studio focused on production, post-production and distribution. BondIt launched in 2013 with a focus on the eliminating the strain in capital from deposits productions leave with guilds to ensure their members are paid in a timely manner. 
	

	Sandaled Kid launched in 2020 with a focus on micro- and mid-budget genre films, particularly action and horror. Bressack’s credits include “Darkness of Man,” “Hot Seat” and “Fortress.”

schema.headline: BondIt, Buffalo 8 and Sandaled Kid Productions Team Up on High-Concept Horror Film Slate (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Girls’ Shocker: Lena Dunham Sets Revival at HBO With Allison Williams, Zosia Mamet, Jemima Kirke Returning
description:
A voice of a generation has returned. 

	HBO has greenlit a revival of “Girls,” Lena Dunham‘s beloved and controversial mid-aughts dramedy. The ser
body:
A voice of a generation has returned. 

	HBO has greenlit a revival of “Girls,” Lena Dunham‘s beloved and controversial mid-aughts dramedy. The series will return for a limited, five-episode run with production beginning in 2027 — a decade after the Season 6 finale.

	“Girls” ran on HBO from 2012 to 2017. With Dunham as creator, showrunner and star, the original series followed a group of friends through the misery and dysfunction of their 20s in New York City. All four core cast members are returning for the revival: Dunham as Hannah Horvath, Allison Williams as Marnie Michaels, Jemima Kirke as Jessa Johansson and Zosia Mamet as Shoshanna Shapiro. Additionally, Andrew Rannells reprises the role of Elijah Krantz.
	

	Judd Apatow returns as executive producer on behalf of Apatow Productions alongside Dunham, Ilene S. Landress and Michael P. Cohen of Dunham’s Good Thing Going banner. Williams, Kirke, Mamet and Rannells serve as co-executive producers.


	“We always said we would only return to ‘Girls’ if there was a specific story we were burning to tell,” Dunham said in a statement. “I’ve missed these characters, but for a long time I couldn’t quite picture them in the present day. Then, right around my fortieth birthday, they started talking to me in the shower. And, as you may remember, once this fivesome starts talking it’s pretty hard to get them to stop… It’s rare that you get the chance to return to something that changed your life with the gift of hindsight and a whole new level of gratitude and understanding. I love these girls (and boy), our friends at HBO and all the people who have continued to discover the show and remind us afresh why we do this, which is the joy of being together… and the chance to wear yellow mesh…”
	

	Dunham has expressed openness to the idea of reviving “Girls” multiple times over the years. Speaking to Variety in 2025, she said, “If we had something to say that was really specific and it was a moment in their lives where we felt like revisiting it — like millennial women becoming mothers or stepping into menopause or going to live at old-age homes — I would always want to work with those people again.”

	Musing on each character’s fate, Dunham continued, “Shoshanna was married to, then divorced from, the mayor of New York City, and she runs an athleisure startup that’s zero-waste. Marnie — it’s third marriage. She still sings, but I think Marnie really needs to take it to Sex and Love Addicts Anonymous. Jessa is unvaccinated and lives on a boat in Croatia. Adam is a cult theater actor, and he’s probably living in Berlin, and Ray is still on city council and running his coffee shop and doing better than anyone. Elijah is the fourth lead on a sitcom, making a good amount of money and still looking for love in all the wrong places.” About her own character, Dunham added, “She teaches at Bard and loves raising her son. She probably has a girlfriend who’s, like, a chef. And she’s less obsessed with being famous. That is where I feel that she would land.” Read her full essay about the revival here.

	While it was a frequent topic of debate during its time on the air, “Girls” is often named one of the greatest television shows of all time, including by Variety in 2023: “The pilot positioned a quartet of downwardly mobile, alliteratively named New York millennials as a counterpoint to ‘Sex and the City,’ trading aspiration for closely observed cringe. That Dunham, just 26 when the show premiered, was so consistently conflated with her character is at once a product of misogyny and a testament to her performance.” The series, which earned 19 Emmy nominations and two wins during its run, has received significant renewed appreciation over the last few years.

	Two names from the original “Girls” team were noticeably absent from HBO’s press release about the revival: Adam Driver, who starred as Hannah’s on-and-off love interest Adam, and co-showrunner and executive producer Jenni Konner. Dunham wrote about negative experiences with both of them in her memoir “Famesick,” released in April of this year.
	

	She alleged that Driver was “verbally aggressive, condescending and physically imposing,” most notably recounting a story in which he threw a chair at a wall next to her because he was angry that she’d forgotten her lines. Driver also took liberties on set that made Dunham feel discomfort and a loss of control: When they filmed their first sex scene, “careful blocking went out the window and he hurled me this way and that,” she said. Driver also allegedly walked out the room when Dunham showed him the completed “Girls” pilot for the first time and ignored her calls for three weeks.

	Konner was a close friend and mentor to Dunham in the early days of “Girls,” but their relationship soured as time passed. For example, Dunham wrote about feeling pressured by Konner to negotiate equal salaries, despite that Dunham created the series and appeared onscreen. When Dunham began to struggle with various health issues and procedures that affected her work schedule, Konner became cold and distant, according to the book. Dunham also wrote that she has no memory of her involvement in the joint statement she and Konner released in 2017 in which they defended “Girls” writer Murray Miller against Aurora Perrineau’s sexual assault allegations. The statement was drafted and published the day after Dunham returned from the hospital after having a hysterectomy, she noted, and she issued an apology shortly after.

	The original “Girls” cast also included Christopher Abbott, Alex Karpovsky, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Jake Lacy and more.

	“We’re thrilled to have Lena turn her gaze from the tumult of one’s twenties to the milestone of turning 40,” reads a statement from Amy Gravitt, executive vice president and head of HBO & HBO Max comedy programming. “To say the world has changed since we last saw Hannah, Marnie, Shoshanna, Jessa and Elijah is a massive understatement, but we know fans — old and new — will be happy to see how they’ve grown and relieved to see that they’re still the ‘Girls’ we knew way back when.”

	See a teaser video featuring Dunham and her castmates below.

title: Where to Buy Tickets for Broadway’s Biggest Shows Through 2027: ‘Evita,’ ‘A Few Good Men,’ ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ and More
description: Broadway is gearing up for a star-studded season, with Hollywood heavyweights, buzzy West End transfers and a slate of high-profile revivals headed
body:
Broadway is gearing up for a star-studded season, with Hollywood heavyweights, buzzy West End transfers and a slate of high-profile revivals headed to New York stages through 2027.

	Among the biggest draws are Julia Louis-Dreyfus, making her Broadway debut alongside Ed Harris and Allison Janney in “Other Desert Cities”; Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell reuniting for a revival of Shakespeare’s “Much Ado About Nothing”; and Rosamund Pike bringing her acclaimed London performance in “Inter Alia” across the Atlantic. Rachel Zegler is also set to lead Jamie Lloyd’s revival of “Evita,” while Billy Crystal returns to the stage with a deeply personal one-man show.


	Musicals are having a particularly big moment, with stage adaptations of Prince’s “Purple Rain” and the “Paddington” books joining revivals of “The Sound of Music” and “The Fantasticks.” Horror fans, meanwhile, can look forward to the Broadway arrival of “Paranormal Activity,” directed by “Sleep No More” creator Felix Barrett.

	Below, find the best way to snag affordable tickets to this season’s current productions:

	
		‘Paranormal Activity’	



	

									Matthew Murphy
	



	SYNOPSIS: The blockbuster horror franchise makes the jump to Broadway in a new supernatural thriller directed by Felix Barrett, the immersive theater pioneer behind “Sleep No More.” Following runs in London and Chicago, the production follows a couple whose attempt to escape their troubled past takes a terrifying turn when they move into a new home.

	THEATER: August Wilson Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Just as he did with Punchdrunk’s long-running date night phenom “Sleep No More,” director Felix Barrett creates an impressive otherworldly, immersive experience. But this time the audience is sitting in place, as he expertly guides the gasps like a sinister maestro, and offers an exhilarating funhouse night in the theater.”

	
		‘School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play’	



	

									Matthew Murphy
	



	SYNOPSIS: Jocelyn Bioh’s acclaimed comedy makes its Broadway debut with Patina Miller, Denée Benton and Jasmine Amy Rogers among the cast. Set at an elite boarding school in Ghana, the play follows a group of teenage girls competing for the chance to represent their country in an international beauty pageant, exposing the complicated politics of friendship, popularity and beauty standards.


	THEATER: Samuel J. Friedman Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “School Girls; or, the African Mean Girls Play” is a joyous and gutting play centering the treasure of Black sisterhood, exceptionalism and the pain and anguish of putting your best foot forward and still falling short of someone much less qualified.”

	
		‘The Imaginary Invalid’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Tony Award winner Bill Irwin stars in a new adaptation of Molière’s classic comedy about a wealthy hypochondriac whose obsession with his health makes him an easy target for the scheming people around him. Irwin also adapted the play, with Brandon J. Dirden directing the Roundabout Theatre Company production.

	THEATER: Todd Haimes Theatre

	
		‘Other Desert Cities’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Julia Louis-Dreyfus makes her Broadway debut alongside Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe in a star-studded revival of Jon Robin Baitz’s family drama. Set during a tense Christmas reunion in Palm Springs, the play follows a daughter whose plans to publish a revealing memoir threaten to expose long-buried family secrets.

	THEATER: Hudson Theatre

	
		‘860’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Billy Crystal returns to Broadway with a deeply personal one-man show inspired by the loss of his longtime Pacific Palisades home in the devastating 2025 Los Angeles wildfires. Directed by Scott Ellis, the autobiographical production blends comedy and reflection as the actor looks back on decades of family memories, love and loss.

	THEATER: Imperial Theatre

	
		‘Operation Mincemeat’	



	

									Julieta Cervantes
	



	SYNOPSIS: The Olivier and Tony Award-winning British musical comedy follows an outrageous real-life World War II intelligence operation involving a corpse, forged documents and a plot to fool the Nazis. After transferring from London’s West End in March 2025, the Broadway production now features Brandon Contreras, Jessi Kirtley, Julia Knitel, Jeff Kready and Amanda Jill Robinson.

	THEATER: Golden Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Think of it as Monty Python on speed, and then throw in some Ealing Studio wit and a bit of ‘Beyond the Fringe’ slyness. Too British? Not if you want to laugh uproariously — and perhaps even unexpectedly shed a tear or two.”

	
		‘A Few Good Men’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Aaron Sorkin’s military courtroom drama returns to Broadway in a new production starring Bradley Whitford and Tom Blyth. Directed by Michael Arden, the revival follows a young Navy lawyer investigating the suspicious death of a Marine at Guantanamo Bay, uncovering a culture of secrecy and abuse within the military.

	THEATER: Vivian Beaumont Theater

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The pace of the Sorkinian banter is meaningful beyond its showiness. It reflects the characters’ intelligence — though they’re at odds, none is the dumb one.”

	
		‘Wanted’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Inspired by the true story of two formerly enslaved sisters, the new musical follows Mary and Martha Clarke as they devise a daring plan to pay off their mother’s sharecropping debt and save her home. Previously staged under the title “Gun & Powder,” the production stars Solea Pfeiffer, Liisi LaFontaine, Luke James and Ledisi, with direction by Stevie Walker-Webb.


	THEATER: James Earl Jones Theatre

	
		‘The Fantasticks’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: One of the longest-running musicals in theater history finally makes its Broadway debut in a reimagined production centered on a gay love story. Directed by Christopher Gattelli, the revival updates the beloved romantic fable about two young lovers whose families secretly scheme to bring them together.

	THEATER: Hayes Theater

	
		‘Much Ado About Nothing’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell star as Shakespeare’s famously sparring lovers Benedick and Beatrice in Jamie Lloyd’s revival of the romantic comedy. Following a London run, the production brings the pair’s battle of wits, romantic misunderstandings and elaborate matchmaking schemes to Broadway.

	THEATER: Winter Garden Theatre

	
		‘Galileo’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Raúl Esparza stars as astronomer Galileo Galilei in a new musical about the scientist whose revolutionary discoveries put him at odds with the Catholic Church. Featuring a book by Danny Strong and music and lyrics by Zoe Sarnak and Michael Weiner, the production arrives on Broadway following its 2024 premiere at Berkeley Repertory Theatre.

	THEATER: Shubert Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The conception of Galileo himself as Renaissance cock-rocker, endlessly pleased with himself — he seems dressed for tomcatting in Anita Yavich’s costumes — might’ve worked in the hands of a performer and show more humorously self-aware. But Esparza’s committed turn doesn’t lend that narcissism much saving irony.”

	
		‘Inter Alia’	



	

									NT Live
	



	SYNOPSIS: Rosamund Pike makes her Broadway debut in Suzie Miller’s legal drama, playing a respected London judge whose carefully balanced personal and professional lives unravel after a devastating family crisis. Directed by Justin Martin, the play arrives in New York following its acclaimed London premiere.

	THEATER: Music Box Theatre
	
		‘Dolly: A True Original Musical’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Dolly Parton’s life and career get the Broadway treatment in a new biographical musical featuring her biggest hits alongside original songs. Written by Parton and Maria S. Schlatter and directed by Bartlett Sher, the show traces the country music legend’s journey from her childhood in Tennessee to international superstardom.

	THEATER: St. James Theatre

	
		‘Awake and Sing!’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Danny Burstein, Micaela Diamond and Jessica Hecht lead a revival of Clifford Odets’ Depression-era family drama. Set in a cramped Bronx apartment, the play follows a working-class Jewish family struggling with financial hardship, generational tensions and the pursuit of the American Dream.

	THEATER: Samuel J. Friedman Theatre

	
		‘Evita’	



	

									Marc Brenner
	



	SYNOPSIS: Rachel Zegler makes her Broadway debut as Eva Perón in Jamie Lloyd’s stripped-down revival of Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice’s musical. Following its London run, the production traces the Argentine First Lady’s rise from poverty to political power, featuring songs including “Don’t Cry for Me Argentina.”

	THEATER: Winter Garden Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “This is, undoubtedly, a technically flawless achievement. And no one will complain about not knowing where their ticket price cash has been spent. But dazzling though it is, there’s something faintly decadent about abandoning the depth of Rice and Lloyd Webber’s strongest achievement for a thrill-ride display.”


	
		‘Purple Rain’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Prince’s iconic 1984 film and album become a Broadway musical following a premiere in the late musician’s hometown of Minneapolis. Directed by Saheem Ali, the production follows an ambitious young musician known as The Kid as he navigates family turmoil, romantic rivalries and the Minneapolis music scene, set to Prince’s legendary songs.

	THEATER: Majestic Theatre
	
		‘Gloria’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Branden Jacobs-Jenkins’ Pulitzer Prize-finalist play makes its Broadway debut in a dark comedy about ambitious editorial assistants at a Manhattan magazine. Directed by Evan Cabnet, the production follows a group of young publishing professionals whose competition for career advancement takes a disturbing turn after a workplace tragedy.

	THEATER: Hayes Theater

	VARIETY REVIEW: The humor is dark and cruel, but terribly funny — until it suddenly isn’t. At which point, the comedy jumps the rails and doesn’t get back on track — until it suddenly does.
	
		‘The Sound of Music’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Rodgers and Hammerstein’s beloved musical returns to Broadway in a new revival directed by Lear deBessonet and starring Jasmine Amy Rogers. Set in Austria on the eve of World War II, the story follows Maria, a spirited young governess who brings music and warmth into the lives of the seven von Trapp children.

	THEATER: Vivian Beaumont Theater

	
		‘Paddington the Musical’	



	

									Sonia Friedman Productions
	



	SYNOPSIS: Everyone’s favorite marmalade-loving bear makes his Broadway debut in a stage musical based on Michael Bond’s children’s books. Arriving from London’s West End, the production follows Paddington as he settles into life with the Brown family in London, with music and lyrics by Tom Fletcher and a book by Jessica Swale.

	THEATER: Al Hirschfeld Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: Furry, funny and fully-formed, the much-anticipated “Paddington” musical has finally arrived and it’s alive not only with joy but that vanishingly rare theatrical quality: completely beguiling charm.

	
		‘The Full Monty’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: The Tony-nominated musical comedy returns to Broadway in a revival directed by Leigh Silverman. Based on the 1997 British film, the show follows six unemployed steelworkers in Buffalo, N.Y., who decide to put on a strip show to make ends meet, discovering unexpected confidence and camaraderie along the way.

	THEATER: Todd Haimes Theatre

	
		‘Oh, Mary!’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: “Saturday Night Live” star Bowen Yang takes on the role of Mary Todd Lincoln in Cole Escola’s irreverent, Tony-winning Broadway comedy. The 80-minute show follows a miserable, booze-soaked First Lady who dreams of becoming a cabaret star while cooped up in the White House during the Civil War.

	WHERE: Lyceum Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “’Oh, Mary!’ is at once campy and complex, a manic bit of extended sketch comedy, but also an unequivocally queer play in which the female characters are played by a trans woman and a nonbinary actor, and the iterations of masculinity are rather gay.”


	
		‘Buena Vista Social Club’	



	

									Ahron R. Foster courtesy of Atlantic Theater Company
	



	SYNOPSIS: A musical about the Cuban artists behind the “Buena Vista Social Club,” an internationally-recognized album of the country’s most popular musical stylings, opened on Broadway in March 2025.


	WHERE: Schoenfeld Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Entering ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ is like stepping into a heady world of the senses, of heightened emotions, and of passionate music and dance. The Social Club was a real place for locals in Havana in the ’50s. Decades later, its music became the source of a Grammy-winning album, then a popular film — and now it’s the most intoxicating and rapturous show of the Broadway season.

	
		‘Stranger Things: The First Shadow’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: Set decades before the events of the “Stranger Things” TV series, “The First Shadow” takes place in the fictional town of Hawkins, Ind. as the Creel family seeks a fresh start, especially Henry, who is eager to escape his troubled past. But when a wave of shocking crimes strikes Hawkins, Henry is forced to consider whether he may have something to do with it.

	WHERE: Marquis Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The show delivers on the spectacle, big time, thanks to the wizardry of the illusions and visual effects designers Jamie Harrison and Chris Fisher — and to the show’s staggering budget. (Netflix is a major producer of the show.)”

	
		Just in Time	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: The immersive Broadway musical charts the life and career of singer Bobby Darin, with Jeremy Jordan currently starring in the title role. Matthew Morrison takes over Oct. 20, followed by Nicholas Christopher on Nov. 10. Featuring a live band and Darin hits including “Splish Splash,” “Beyond the Sea” and “Mack the Knife,” the show transforms Circle in the Square Theatre into an intimate nightclub.

	WHERE: Circle in the Square Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Director Alex Timbers and the book writers fail to go beyond the concert conceit, and never give us a real portrait of Darin or leave us with a clear idea of what we are supposed to think of him.”

	
		‘Maybe Happy Ending’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: The Tony-winning South Korean musical, starring Zachary Noah Piser and Hannah Kevitt, follows two helper robots navigating love and memory. The production opened at the Belasco Theatre in November 2024 with original stars Darren Criss and Helen J. Shen.

	THEATER: Belasco Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “’Maybe Happy Ending’ is an undeniably moving, well-made, adorable musical, and it is a pleasant surprise to see an audience weep at a show about two robots in love.”

	
		‘The Outsiders’	



	

									The Outsiders Broadway
	



	SYNOPSIS: The Tony-winning musical adaptation of S.E. Hinton’s 1967 novel and Francis Ford Coppola’s 1983 film follows a group of working-class teenage “greasers” in Tulsa, Oklahoma, as they navigate friendship, loyalty and a bitter rivalry with the privileged “Socs.” The production currently stars Noah Pacht as Ponyboy Curtis, Dan Berry as Darrel Curtis, Sutton James Kaylor as Sodapop Curtis, Caleb Mathura as Johnny Cade and SeQuoiia as Dallas Winston.

	WHERE: Jacobs Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The production only intermittently rises to the challenge of transforming such familiar material into theater that feels both original and necessary. It packs plenty of heart and soul, but lacks a strong pulse.”
	
		‘The Great Gatsby’	



	

									Matthew Murphy and Evan Zimmerman
	



	SYNOPSIS: The musical adaptation of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s classic novel now stars Ryan McCartan as Jay Gatsby and China Anne McClain as Daisy Buchanan, alongside Corbin Bleu as Nick Carraway. Set amid the excess of the Roaring Twenties, the production brings the doomed romance to Broadway with a score by Jason Howland and Nathan Tysen.


	WHERE: The Broadway Theater

	VARIETY REVIEW: “For any fan of ‘The Great Gatsby’ it’s likely you’ll have moments of wanting more, of missing out on all the subtext, grit, and suffering beneath the sequins.”
	
		‘& Juliet’	



	

									Matthew Murphy
	



	SYNOPSIS: Created by the Emmy-winning writer of “Schitt’s Creek,” this acclaimed musical-comedy imagines what would happen if Shakespeare’s Juliet didn’t “end it all over Romeo.”

	WHERE: Stephen Sondheim Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “’& Juliet’ is exactly the show Broadway needs right now: fun, exuberant, supremely joyful, hilarious, and excellently performed by a talented and diverse cast. The amount of confetti may be gratuitous (they seem to be trying to outdo “Moulin Rouge!”), but honestly, why not?”
	
		‘MJ’	



	

									Matthew Murphy
	



	SYNOPSIS: The Tony-winning jukebox musical traces Michael Jackson’s career through rehearsals for his 1992 Dangerous World Tour, featuring nearly 40 songs from his catalog, including “Billie Jean,” “Beat It” and “Thriller.” Directed and choreographed by Christopher Wheeldon, the production opened on Broadway in 2022.

	WHERE: Neil Simon Theater

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Packed with nearly 40 hits from Michael Jackson’s irresistible catalogue, the Broadway production from director and choreographer Christopher Wheeldon is not so much a biomusical as a high-shine and surface-skimming rehabilitation tour for its late subject, flattening rather than reckoning with his complex legacy.”
	
		‘Six: The Musical’	



	

									Courtesy of Liz Lauren
	



	SYNOPSIS: After earning a million dollars during its first week of previews at the Brooks Atkinson Theatre, “Six” was hours away from officially opening before the COVID-19 shutdown went into effect on March 12. This wildly original stage production is like watching a pop concert starring the six ex-wives of Henry VIII.

	WHERE: Lena Horne Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Audience interest in this competitive concert concept could easily wear out its welcome but the musical variety, bite-sized storytelling and unstoppable performances keep the entertainment level high as the musical subversively builds in emotional depth.”
	
		‘Wicked’	



	

									Joan Marcus
	



	SYNOPSIS: A prequel of sorts to “The Wizard of Oz,” “Wicked” recounts the happenings in Oz before Dorothy sauntered down the yellow brick road and tells the story of how a green-skinned woman named Elphaba becomes the Wicked Witch of the West. With classic songs like “Defying Gravity” and “Popular,” it’s one of the most beloved shows on Broadway.

	WHERE: Gershwin Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “‘Wicked’ is stridently earnest one minute, self-mocking the next; a fantastical allegory about the perils of fascism in one scene, a Nickelodeon special about the importance of inner beauty in another.”

	
		 ‘Hadestown’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: The Tony-winning musical, written by celebrated singer-songwriter Anais Mitchell. The acclaimed show is a love story at its heart, following the mythical tales of two intertwining couples, Orpheus and Eurydice, and King Hades and his wife Persephone.


	WHERE: Walter Kerr Theater

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The storytelling is spare, but the visuals say it all, helped along by the melodious voice and slip-sliding dance moves of the indomitable André De Shields as the swift-footed god Hermes, as well as by the three gorgeous, golden-throated Fates played by Jewelle Blackman, Yvette Gonzalez-Nacer and Kay Trinidad.”
	
		‘Aladdin’	



	

									Deen van Meer
	



	SYNOPSIS: The musical based on the 1992 Disney animated film at Broadway’s New Amsterdam Theatre

	WHERE: New Amsterdam Theatre
	
		‘Chicago’	



	

	



	SYNOPSIS: The longest-running American musical in Broadway history has returned with the razzle dazzle. The Tony-winning revival tells the story of two women in Chicago who will use absolutely anything at their disposal to stay on the front page of the local newspaper, from behind prison bars.

	WHERE: Ambassador Theatre

	
		‘Hamilton’	



	

									Courtesy of Matthew Murphy
	



	SYNOPSIS: Lin Manuel Miranda’s hip-hop musical tribute to one of our illustrious Founding Fathers was an immediate sensation upon its 2015 debut, and it’s still going strong on Broadway with a new cast. If you can’t make it in person, Disney+ has a live recording of the production with the original cast, including Miranda. 

	WHERE: Richard Rodgers Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Like any true landmark, ‘Hamilton’ stands up to repeated viewings. After six months, the show’s initial impact hasn’t dulled a bit; in fact, the qualities that made it so extraordinary the first time around are all the more striking.”
	
		‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’	



						
			
	

									Manuel Harlan
	



	SYNOPSIS: Based on an original story written by J.K Rowling, this adapted play takes place 19 years after the events of “Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows.”

	WHERE: Lyric Theatre 

	VARIETY REVIEW: “Best of all, there’s a set of bookcases in the Hogwarts library that keep swallowing and spitting out unwary readers. But for all its inventive stagecraft devices, the show has a plot that really works as an extension of the Potter saga.”
	
		‘The Lion King’	



	

									Courtesy of Joan Marcus
	



	SYNOPSIS: King Mufasa, Simba, Scar and the rest of the animals from the Pride Lands of Africa.

	WHERE: Minskoff Theatre

	
		‘The Book of Mormon’	



						
			
	

									Joan Marcus
	




	SYNOPSIS: This hilarious, Tony-winning musical follows two Latter-day Saints missionaries as they attempt to preach the teachings of their religion to a the inhabitants of a remote Ugandan village.   

	WHERE: Eugene O’Neill Theatre

	VARIETY REVIEW: “The cast shows no evidence of being second tier, and production values are as lavish and performance style as crisp as at the show’s nativity. As long as you don’t go expecting the Second Coming, you’re unlikely to be let down by this breathlessly funny, solidly crafted musical satire.”

title: Druski Hosting ‘SNL’ Is the Show’s Most Interesting Move in Years
description: As “Saturday Night Live” trudges on this season with a little-known cast, uneven sketches and yet another horrendous appearance by obvious misogyni
body:
As “Saturday Night Live” trudges on this season with a little-known cast, uneven sketches and yet another horrendous appearance by obvious misogynist Shane Gillis, news that comedian and internet personality Druski, aka Drew Desbordes, will host the Nov. 7 episode suddenly gives me hope. I think it’s the most interesting thing “SNL” has done in years.

	Admittedly, I’m not the biggest “Saturday Night Live” fan. I’ve tuned in rarely over the years, usually only when an actor or artist I find fascinating hosts. In the last decade, it’s been rare: Eddie Murphy hosting in 2019, Megan Thee Stallion appearing in the iconic “Girl Talk” sketch with Ego Nwodim and Dave Chappelle’s 2025 appearance, where he paid homage to his beloved sketch comedy series “Chapelle’s Show.” But I’ve mostly had very little interest in tuning in over the years. 
	

	The idea of bringing Druski to Studio 8H at least feels like a cutting-edge thing that the “SNL” of old might have done. The 32-year-old comedian is the first content creator to ever host the show, which has sparked a lot of kerfuffle (some rightfully so) about influencers stepping into spaces previously reserved for “true celebrities.” But I would argue that Druski has never been an influencer. He has always been a comedian first, an artist who honed his craft by posting short skits on his Instagram page and eventually building an organic audience of 35+ million followers and billions of views across Instagram, TikTok and YouTube.


	Until more recently, mainstream studios and streamers have ignored Druski in favor of blondes who’ve never read a book. However, Druski has been a name in the Black community for nearly a decade. Just a few years into posting, the Maryland-born comedian appeared in music videos for major hip-hop artists like Drake and Lil Yachty. Instead of using a musician as the opening act for their 2021 tour, rappers J. Cole and 21 Savage had Druski open for them. In addition to his comedy work, Druski created “Coulda Been Records,” which allowed artists to join his Instagram Live posts and collaborate. He had a starring role in Peacock’s 2023 film “Praise This” opposite Chloe Bailey, and in 2025 launched the 10-city arena tour Coulda Fest, which sold out immediately.
	

	However, it’s Druski’s ability to put his finger on the pulse of societal touchstones with elaborate, hilarious and self-funded skits that makes him almost a singular entity in the comedy space today. While older comedians regurgitate tired material or appear in the prequels and sequels of the latest recycled IP, Druski calls out the hypocrisy of megachurches and takes Erika Kirk to task while indicting white supremacy and American conservatism. On a more granular level, his work has commented on the horrors of 21st-century dating, “hat fishing” (when men hide their balding hairlines under fitted caps), and the terror that we all feel at airports when encountering aggressive and impatient TSA agents. Druski’s comedy embodies what it means to be a young American at this particular moment.

	Though his perspective is often from a Black lens, American culture overall is typically siphoned from Black culture before moving into the mainstream. Because Black people have been so subjugated in this country via slavery, Jim Crow, racism and now the Trump administration, knowing how to weave in and out of white spaces is essential to Black survival. However, that revolving door does not work the other way. As a result, the mainstream often has blind spots or is years late in “discovering” Black talent. 

	It’s the same reason why so many people publicly admonished Will Smith’s actions at the 2024 Oscars while Black people collectively still feel that Chris Rock deserved that slap. There’s a reason comparing Taylor Swift to Beyoncé never made sense, or why, when DEI is erased from boardrooms, marketing campaigns like Sydney Sweeney’s “Good Genes” are greenlit. Or, that somebody has the idea that Kendall Jenner is suddenly the person to solve racism with a Pepsi. It’s the same reason why movies, commercials and television have felt stale and uninspired for years. Innovation can only happen when new ideas and perspectives are taken into account.

	For Black talent like Druski — and even Issa Rae before him — rejection means taking things into their own hands and building an audience organically. It’s only later that the mainstream wakes up and comes knocking after something has already been built. In fact, “SNL” is rather late in bringing Druski to its stage: In June, he hosted the 2026 BET Awards, becoming the youngest host in the show’s 25-year history. He’s also slated to star opposite Chris Pine and Emma Stone in the upcoming film “The Catch.”
	

	Druski has worked for years to build his own platform and digital leverage, which extends well beyond the confining term of “influencer.” He has been a shining star in the Black community for years; everyone else — including “SNL” — is just now catching up.

title: Battle of the Booths: Paramount Brings its Iconic Arch to Cannes as Eye-Catching Mipcom Stands Reflect Market Realities
description: Step outside Le Palais des Festivals in Cannes this week, where Mipcom is in full swing, and you might do a double take. Because nestled between th
body:
Step outside Le Palais des Festivals in Cannes this week, where Mipcom is in full swing, and you might do a double take. Because nestled between the conference center and the French Riviera is an exact (well, 90% scale) replica of Paramount Studios’ iconic Bronson Gate.

	The model arch, affixed via cleverly concealed aluminium and wood scaffolding, is located at the entrance to the studio’s 6,000-square foot exhibition tent at the international content marketplace. “[We’ve had] a lot of comments, a lot of what looks like selfies — people taking photos in front of the gate,” says Lisa Lasarenko, Paramount’s SVP for marketing and creative services, who oversaw the build. “Because it’s a little bit of Hollywood in Cannes.”
	

	On either side, the replica gate is bordered by a trompe l’oeil print of the Paramount Studios soundstages emblazoned with posters of some of the big ticket titles the company is selling at this year’s market, which is taking place Oct. 12-15, including “The Angry Birds Movie 3,” the Johnny Depp-led “Ebenezer” and “NCIS: New York.”


	“We wanted to do something different,” Lasarenko says of the project, which took design agency Glow Studios around three weeks to build and ship over from the U.K. Glow founder James Schnauer even flew out to L.A. to photograph the arch so he could “reverse engineer the detail” and make a 3D-printed model. (The finished result is so detailed it includes the intricate filigrees found on the original.) “It feels like you’re having an experience and bring our clients something that they can’t get anywhere else,” says Lasarenko.
	



	

									Banijay
	



	Paramount’s is not the only stand-out booth at this year’s confab, which is organized by RX France. The newly-expanded Banijay Entertainment, who occupy a prime position directly in front of the Palais on the Croisette, have returned with the same two-storey, wooden stand they first debuted in 2022, in keeping with its environmental mission.

	Designed by architect Nicola Spinetto and created by Romain Larue from Orati, the eco-friendly structure — which resembles a chalet and is dubbed Banijay House — includes meeting rooms, a reception area and several terraces. Between Mipcoms it is flat-packed and kept in storage just outside Cannes. “We don’t use it for any other market,” says Andrew Dickens, Banijay’s communications and marketing EVP.

	Meanwhile, overlooking the Riviera behind the Palais is Fremantle’s booth, which this year has been themed to reflect one of its biggest titles — “Baywatch.” Kitted out like a beachhouse, the exhibition stand is decorated with the show’s classic red life preservers, surfboards and even a lifeguard’s hut on the patio. (Fremantle’s “Baywatch”-emblazoned red tote bags, previously available at the booth’s front desk, have proved so popular they’ve been limited to clients only).

	On the opposite end of the strip outside the Palais, toy brands Mattel, Hasbro and Pokemon occupy three adjacent stands. Mattel have opted for a simpler design look — a red tent with a large brand logo and some matching cushions scattered on the patio chairs outside — while next door Pokemon have gone for the “more is more” approach, with a booth covered in images of its multitudinous critters plus a small hedge pruned to look like a Pokeball by the door.

	Although the stands inside the Palais are not as eye-catching (both Sony and Disney are tucked away on the third floor in bare-bones appointment-only booths), the country pavilions have added some pizazz to their exhibition spaces: Singapore’s stand is covered in dozens of orchids, bringing some much needed nature to the convention center’s otherwise stark basement, while China has been wowing passers-by with a full-size AI-powered humanoid robot on its reception. Billed as “Your 24/7 productivity partner,” the Agibot A3 has been chatting to attendees in French, English and Cantonese.
	



	

					Mipcom (© S. d’Halloy / Image & Co)
									© S. d’HALLOY / IMAGE & CO
	



	While the exhibitor stands are designed to be attention-grabbing, they also tell a story about the state of the industry. Five years ago, the first post-Covid Mipcom was “an understated affair,” as Variety noted in its 2021 market wrap, with few participants outside of Europe (overall it was estimated there were only about 4,500 attendees that year compared with 12,000 pre-pandemic) and modest booths. While the confab bounced back over the next few years (albeit dropping its spring counterpart MipTV along the way), the streaming wars saw studios largely hoarding content for their own global platforms, meaning there was little need to reel in international buyers, reducing the need for show-stopping floor space.

	Although the industry has pivoted back to licensing, it’s consolidation that is now impacting the landscape — and the effects reverberate on the market floor. As part of Banijay and All3Media’s merger, which closed in July, the new joint entity inherited All3Media’s stand, which has been renamed Banijay Terrace and is being used for overspill. But Dickens is clear this will be “for one year only” – resulting in an empty space Mipcom will need to fill in 2027.

	It remains to be seen whether Warner Bros. Discovery, who this year are in their usual beachfront spot in Ciro’s, will have to share tent-space next year with their new sister brand Paramount, following the recent acquisition by Skydance, or whether the brands will be permitted to exhibit independently.

	In the meantime, what is Lasarenko planning to do with the replica Paramount arch? “We’re gonna keep it,” she says. “And find ways to use it.”

title: Vancouver Film Festival Audience Award Winners: ’I Play Rocky,’ ‘Ceremony’ Among Big Wins
description: Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky” has won the Audience Award in the Galas & Special Presentations category at the 2026 Vancouver International Film F
body:
Peter Farrelly’s “I Play Rocky” has won the Audience Award in the Galas & Special Presentations category at the 2026 Vancouver International Film Festival (VIFF).

	The film, which tells the underdog story behind Sylvester Stallone’s journey to make and star in “Rocky,” was among 10 titles selected by audiences as favorites across the festival’s programming sections — including international cinema, emerging filmmakers and Canadian features.
	

	Banchi Hanuse’s documentary “Ceremony,” which hadpreviously took home the the juried Tides Award, won in the Showcase category. It follows the disappearance of the ooligan, a culturally significant fish in Bella Coola, and the Nuxalk Nation’s efforts to understand its decline.


	Former Pixar animator Louis Clichy’s “Iron Boy,” which explores themes of disability and agricultural modernization, took the Panorama prize. The Vanguard award went to Fernanda Salgado’s “Ana, En Passant,” an animated drama about a young Black woman returning to her late grandmother’s native town in Brazil.

	Cody Lightning’s hockey drama “Smudge the Blades,” following a team of Indigenous youth in Northern Alberta, earned the Northern Lights award.

	Other category winners include Faraz Shariat’s “Prosecution” (Focus on New German Cinema: Extreme Tension), Asmahan Bkerat’s “Concrete Land” (Insights), Otilia Portillo Padua’s “Daughters of the Forest” (Spectrum), Rebecca Tansley’s “Tenor: My Name Is Parti” (Portraits), and Marco Nguyen and Nicolas Athané’s “Jim Queen” (Altered States).
	

	The 45th Vancouver International Film Festival ran Oct. 1-11 and included 162 features and 91 short films, representing 76 countries.

title: Bernie Orenstein, Co-Writer of ‘That Girl’ and ‘The New Dick Van Dyke Show,’ Dies at 95
description:
Bernie Orenstein, the co-writer and co-producer of “The New Dick Van Dyke Show,” died on Sept. 14, his family confirmed. He was 95.

	The televisio
body:
Bernie Orenstein, the co-writer and co-producer of “The New Dick Van Dyke Show,” died on Sept. 14, his family confirmed. He was 95.

	The television comedy writer and producer frequently collaborated with his partner, Saul Turteltaub, whom he wrote and produced TV hits such as “The New Dick Van Dyke Show,” the 1970s follow-up to the original hit series, “That Girl” “The Beautiful Phyllis Diller Show,” “Kate & Allie,” “What’s Happening!!” and “Cosby.” The duo also worked on “Sanford and Son.” Orenstein previously shared that the show’s star Redd Foxx was very protective of “the two white Jewish guys writing a Black show.”
	

	Throughout his 40-year career, Orenstein worked with notable names such as Joan Rivers, Dean Martin, Judy Garland, Dick Van Dyke, Marlo Thomas and Bing Crosby.


	Outside of his work on television, Orenstein dedicated his time to serving as a mentor and educator to rising writers and producers at Long Island University Brooklyn’s TV Writers Studio MFA program.

	In his 2016 interview with the Television Academy Foundation, Orenstein reflected on his career and shared he was the most proud of everything he’s done. “I’ve hung around a long time,” he said.

	When asked how he’d like to be remembered, Orenstein said, “By the body of work and the fact that I never hurt anybody.”

	Orenstein was born in Toronto in 1931 and later moved to New York City to write for the reality series “Candid Camera.” He then wrote for “The Hollywood Palace” before beginning his partnership with Turteltaub.
	

	He is survived by his wife, Barbara Rhoades Orenstein; his children, Lisa, Barbara, Jenny and Alec; eight grandchildren; and four great-grandchildren.

body:
'RuPaul's Drag Race' Lucian Piane
                          Death Ruled Accidental

                            12:23 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Lucian Piane's manner of death has been revealed ... and officials have ruled the "RuPaul's Drag Race" alum's passing an accident ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner, Lucian died from blunt trauma Monday at age 46. His place of death is listed as a street, and his body is now "ready for release" ... though the case remains open.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Lucian was struck by a car in Glendale early Monday morning. Firefighters tried to save him, but he was pronounced dead at the scene.
      

            His death came after a troubling weekend that included two run-ins with Glendale police ... first on Saturday for allegedly being under the influence of a controlled substance, then again Sunday for allegedly assaulting a police officer or emergency worker.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            He was cited and released both times ... and was scheduled to appear in court Monday, the same day he died.
      
    
            Lucian was best known for his work as a songwriter, producer, and judge on "RuPaul's Drag Race," contributing to the show's music across multiple seasons.

body:
'Pioneer Woman' Ree Drummond
                          Foster Son Facing More Trouble After Meth Bust

                            11:10 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            'Pioneer Woman' Ree Drummond's foster son, Jamar Goff, is facing more legal trouble after his recent drug arrest ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court docs, obtained by TMZ, Alabama prosecutors asked to revoke 23-year-old Jamar's bond from a 2025 criminal case, citing domestic violence allegations. The judge signed off on an arrest warrant a few days later.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The move comes after Jamar was recently arrested in September for meth possession after cops say they found him seemingly asleep on a bench at the University of Alabama at Birmingham. Officers say he told them he was waiting to buy "ice," which the docs note is a nickname for meth.
      

            Cops say Jamar ran from the officer but was later tracked down … and the officer says he found over 1.8 grams of meth on Jamar, who is still in custody and has yet to bond out.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As TMZ first reported, Jamar claimed to be homeless in court docs. He checked into rehab a couple of months before his latest arrest.
      
    
            Jamar reportedly became a part of Ree's family back in 2018.

title: Halle Berry Fights to Keep Son From Testifying, Accuses Ex Olivier of Coaching Him
description:
Halle Berry to Ex Olivier Martinez
                          Quit Coaching Our Son for Court!!!
body:
Halle Berry to Ex Olivier Martinez
                          Quit Coaching Our Son for Court!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 13, 2026
                            12:26 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Halle Berry doesn't want her son taking the witness stand in her nasty custody battle with Olivier Martinez ... because she believes her ex-husband has been coaching the boy on what to say.
